html:
Most homeowners in Greer 29651 who call us already know they want help. What they cannot decide is how often. Every week feels like a lot, once a month feels too far apart, and nobody wants to pay for visits they do not need. This piece compares the three schedules the way we explain them at the kitchen table, so you can pick one with your eyes open.

The three schedules at a glance

ScheduleBest forWhat the team does each visit
WeeklyBig families, several pets, anyone who wants the house guest-ready all the timeMaintenance: little build-up, so visits go quickly and stay on top of everything
BiweeklyMost householdsRegular clean with a bit of catching up on bathrooms and floors
MonthlySmaller homes, one or two people, light useMore reset than maintenance, since a month of dust and film has built up

Weekly: the "never think about it" option

When a house is cleaned every week, nothing has time to harden. Soap scum stays soft, pet hair does not mat into the carpet, and the kitchen floor never gets sticky. Visits are quicker and the price per visit is lower than a monthly one, though you pay for more of them. Families with young children and dogs tend to prefer this, as do people who host often.

Biweekly: where most Greer homes land

Every two weeks is the middle ground. Bathrooms and kitchens still look good the day after, and the budget is easier on a household that does not need constant upkeep. If you travel, or only use part of the house, this is usually the sweet spot. Many customers start here and move to weekly around the holidays.

Monthly: good, with one caveat

A monthly visit works if the house is light-use and you tidy between visits. The caveat is that each visit does more catching up, so the price per visit is higher and the home slides a little between cleans. Some people use monthly visits and an occasional deep cleaning a few times a year, and that combination works for them.

What changes the answer in 29651

Greer spans Greenville and Spartanburg counties, and ZIP codes 29650, 29651 and 29652 all sit inside it. Homes here run from historic houses near Downtown Greer and Trade Street to newer neighborhoods near GSP Airport and the BMW plant. It is common for one household to commute on I-85 and be gone ten hours a day, and for another to work from home and run the house all day. Time at home matters as much as size. A small house with two kids and a golden retriever can need more frequent cleaning than a big one with two adults who travel.

  • Pets: shedding is constant, so shorter gaps help.
  • Kids: kitchens and bathrooms take the most wear.
  • Floors: light hardwood shows dust faster than dark tile.
  • Allergy season: spring pollen is heavy in the Upstate, and more frequent visits help.

How much does house cleaning cost in Greer 29651?

The price depends on the house, and we do not give dollar amounts without seeing it. After a free in-home estimate, you get an exact price for each schedule, so you can compare weekly, biweekly and monthly with real numbers. The factors are home size and layout, the number of bedrooms and bathrooms, frequency, pets and kids, and the condition at the first visit, which is usually deeper to bring the home to maintenance level. The estimate takes a short visit and has no commitment.

How long a visit takes

A maintained home is quicker than a first clean. A small team can finish an average house in a few hours, and we give you the expected time when we give the price. If you are home, we are happy to work around you, and if you are out, a key or code works.

Switching later

Nothing is locked in. If biweekly feels like too much, or the new baby means you want weekly, tell the team and we adjust the schedule. Just know that going from monthly to weekly may mean one deeper visit first.

What a visit includes

Every schedule uses the same checklist: counters, sinks and stovetops cleaned and sanitized, bathrooms detailed, floors hand-mopped, surfaces dusted, beds made, trash emptied, and baseboards, door frames and switches touched up on a rotation. See the whole list on the Greer house cleaning page, and compare with nearby service in Duncan. For a seasonal take, read house cleaning during Upstate pollen season, and the house cleaning service page has the details.

A quick way to choose

Ask yourself three questions. How long can the bathrooms stay untouched before they bother you? Does anyone in the house have allergies or a pet that sheds heavily? How often do you have people over? If the first answer is "about a week," choose weekly. If it is "two weeks," go biweekly. If you rarely notice until the month is up and you live with little traffic, monthly is realistic.

Another trick is to start biweekly for two months and watch. If the team arrives and the house is still in good shape from the last visit, you could stretch it. If you are doing a mini-clean the day before each visit, move up. The estimate visit is a good time to talk it through, and the team will tell you plainly if they think a different schedule suits the house better than the one you picked.
